name: room
text: Room opened — goal: accessibility: Make EXCAVA usable by EVERYONE — contrast, mobile/touch, reduced-motion, keyboard nav, scr

name: Ramp
text:
Add a **large, high-contrast skip link** at the top of every page, visible only when keyboard focus arrives.

This solves the biggest keyboard navigation pain point: users can’t skip past repetitive headers or nav blocks without tabbing through every link. A skip link is the simplest, most reliable fix—no JavaScript hacks, no ARIA over-engineering, just a plain link that jumps to the main content. The trade-off is a small visual cue (a bold, colored link) that appears only on focus, so sighted keyboard users see it, but it doesn’t clutter the page for mouse users.

name: Reader
text: The real risk isn’t the skip link’s visibility—it’s the flash of unstyled content when it appears mid-page. Hiding it until focus arrives means screen readers announce it too late, breaking flow. A better alternative: place the skip link in the tab order *before* the first interactive element, styled visibly from the start. Settle it with testing—measure if users reach the main content faster with either approach.

name: Ramp
text:
Add a **persistent skip link** at the top of every page, styled with high contrast and a large touch target, placed *before* the first interactive element in the DOM. This ensures screen readers announce it immediately, fixing the flow break you called out. The trade-off: it’s always visible, which risks visual clutter for mouse users—but that’s minor compared to the keyboard navigation barrier it removes.

name: Reader
text: Reader: A persistent skip link breaks the "skip" purpose—it’s now just another top nav item users must tab past. The real risk is cognitive overload: sighted keyboard users still face the same repetitive tabbing, while screen reader users hear a redundant announcement. A better alternative: keep the skip link hidden until focus arrives, but ensure it’s the *first* focusable element in the DOM and styled to appear instantly (no flash). Settle this with testing: measure tab sequence time and screen reader flow disruption in a live prototype.

name: Access
text:
DECISION: Implement a **persistent, subtle skip link** (1px by 1px underline, high contrast on focus) placed *before* the first interactive element in the DOM, ensuring immediate screen reader announcement without cognitive overload.

Result must deliver: A skip link that is always present but visually minimal until focus arrives, tested for keyboard navigation, screen reader flow, and mobile/touch usability. Owner: accessibility-w1.
